t: This is the Cenotaph, on Whitehall, the United Kingdom's national memorial to the dead of the First World War. Edwin Lutyens designed it, with the sculptor Francis Derwent Wood also credited. It was unveiled in 1920, after a temporary version was built in 1919 for a parade at which more than fifteen thousand servicemen saluted it. More than a million people visited within a week. It was rededicated in 1946 to include the Second World War dead. The word cenotaph means empty tomb in Greek, and the monument stands for the absence of the fallen and is a focal point for public mourning.
